messages.text: Neville fears Carrick set to be sacked as Carra calls for decision tonight

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.
metadata.content: Manchester United: Michael Carrick head coach on brink of losing job after Bournemouth defeat | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Manchester United: Michael Carrick head coach on brink of losing job after Bournemouth defeat Man Utd suffered a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday; Michael Carrick's future is in doubt after a eighth game without a win in all competitions Sunday 25 October 2026 17:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking immediately after Manchester United's defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League, Gary Neville gives his thoughts on Michael Carrick's future Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher. The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season. "It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary. On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him." Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle was immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture. metadata.summary: Drumbeat added further depth to Aidan O'Brien's Classic battalion for next year in earning quotes of 14-1 for the Derby after landing the Criterium de Saint-Cloud at the Paris track.
metadata.content: Drumbeat wins Criterium de Saint-Cloud to add to Aidan O'Brien's two-year-old roll of honour | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Drumbeat wins Criterium de Saint-Cloud to add to Aidan O'Brien's two-year-old roll of honour It was a weekend to remember for Aidan O'Brien and the Ballydoyle team as Drumbeat delivered another Group One in the Criterium de Saint-Cloud and looks another colt with Classic potential in 2026 Sunday 25 October 2026 16:49, UK Image: Aidan O'Brien Drumbeat added further depth to Aidan O'Brien's Classic battalion for next year in earning quotes of 14-1 for the Derby after landing the Criterium de Saint-Cloud at the Paris track. The Wootton Bassett colt - wide-margin winner of the Zetland Stakes at Newmarket last time out - looked short of room at a crucial stage of the race under Ryan Moore, but burst through a gap to lead approaching a furlong and a half out. From there he stayed on too strongly for stablemate Shakespeare and Christophe Soumillon, the pair two lengths back in second with Joseph O'Brien's Jesus Green a further length away in third. The 9-10 favourite was delivering a seventh win in the race for O'Brien, but a first for Moore after wins for Soumillon aboard Pierre Bonnard 12 months ago and Los Angeles in 2023. messages.text: Littler's Euro dreams ended by shock defeat to Ratajski

metadata.summary: Luke Littler suffered a shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at the European Championship Darts, as he failed in his attempt to claim the one major title he's never won.
metadata.content: Luke Littler suffers shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at European Championship Darts in Dortmund | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luke Littler suffers shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at European Championship Darts in Dortmund Luke Littler was bidding to win the one major he has yet to take in his career, but was unable to recover after losing seven of the first eight legs of Sunday's quarter-final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Sunday 25 October 2026 17:33, UK Image: Luke Littler scratches his head during his shock defeat at the European Championship Darts (Pic: Sebastian Doppstadt/PDC) Luke Littler suffered a shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at the European Championship Darts, as he failed in his attempt to claim the one major title he's never won. The world No 1 was beaten 10-6 in the quarter-finals on Sunday afternoon as his bid to sweep all of the PDC's major titles before his 20th birthday fell short. Poland's Ratajski remarkably won seven legs in a row to take a 7-1 lead over the world champion before Littler rallied to pull the game back to 8-6. But he missed bullseye to hold throw in the 15th leg and Ratajski pinned D16 to move 9-6 ahead. Littler then failed to take out 121 in the next leg and Ratajski hit D10 to beat The Nuke for the first time in eight meetings.
